hypothesis: Patients whose tumor samples were collected prospectively have higher tumor mutational burdens than those collected retrospectively.

experiment_plan.objective: To test whether tissue collection strategy influences measured TMB.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv. 2. Compute per‐patient TMB (mutation counts). 3. From clinical data, extract tissue_prospective_collection status (YES vs NO). 4. Merge TMB with prospective_collection status. 5. Compare TMB distributions between YES and NO groups using Wilcoxon rank‐sum test. 6. Fit a linear regression of TMB on prospective_collection status adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender. 7. Create a boxplot of TMB by collection strategy.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Wilcoxon test statistic and p‐value comparing TMB in Prospective vs Retrospective samples.  • Regression coefficients, standard errors, p‐values, and R² for the model.  • Boxplot of TMB stratified by tissue_prospective_collection.  • Merged dataset preview: patient_id, prospective_collection status, and TMB.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# Compute Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB) per patient
tmb = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='TMB')

# Prepare clinical subset with collection strategy, age, and gender
clin_sub = clinical[['submitter_id', 'tissue_prospective_collection', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender']]
clin_sub = clin_sub.rename(columns={
    'submitter_id': 'patient_id',
    'tissue_prospective_collection': 'prospective'
})

# Merge TMB with clinical data, fill missing TMB with 0
df = clin_sub.merge(tmb, on='patient_id', how='left')
df['TMB'] = df['TMB'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Drop records with missing collection strategy
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['prospective'])

# Split groups
group_yes = df_clean.loc[df_clean['prospective'] == 'YES', 'TMB']
group_no = df_clean.loc[df_clean['prospective'] == 'NO', 'TMB']

# Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U)
u_stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(group_yes, group_no, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test between prospective=YES and NO: U = {u_stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4g}\n")

# Linear regression: TMB ~ prospective + age_at_diagnosis + gender
# Convert prospective and gender to categorical
df_clean['prospective'] = df_clean['prospective'].astype('category')
df_clean['gender'] = df_clean['gender'].astype('category')
model = smf.ols('TMB ~ C(prospective) + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=df_clean).fit()

# Regression summary
print("Linear regression results:")
coef_table = pd.DataFrame({
    'coef': model.params,
    'std_err': model.bse,
    'p_value': model.pvalues
})
print(coef_table)
print(f"R-squared: {model.rsquared:.3f}\n")

# Boxplot of TMB by collection strategy
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.title('TMB by Tissue Collection Strategy')
plt.xlabel('Prospective Collection')
plt.ylabel('TMB')

# Using pandas boxplot
df_clean.boxplot(column='TMB', by='prospective', grid=False)
plt.suptitle('')  # Remove automatic title
plt.show()

# Preview merged dataset
print("Preview of merged data (first 10 rows):")
print(df_clean[['patient_id', 'prospective', 'TMB']].head(10))

The experiment successfully tested whether tumor mutational burden (TMB) differs by tissue collection strategy. Key results:

• Wilcoxon rank-sum test (prospective=YES vs NO): U = 18823.50, p = 1.74 × 10⁻⁸, indicating a highly significant difference in TMB distributions between groups.  
• Linear regression (TMB ~ prospective + age_at_diagnosis + gender):
  – R² = 0.020 (very low explained variance)
  – Intercept = 41.49 (p = 0.938)
  – Prospective (YES vs NO) coefficient = –255.58 (p = 0.340, not significant)
  – Gender (male vs female) coefficient = 612.15 (p = 0.0237)
  – Age at diagnosis coefficient = 15.72 (p = 0.0618)
• Boxplot of TMB by collection strategy shows similar median and IQR for YES vs NO, with outliers especially in the YES group.  
• Merged dataset preview confirms correct patient-level TMB values for both groups.

Despite the significant unadjusted Wilcoxon test, the adjusted regression found no significant effect of prospective collection on TMB and the model explains only ~2% of variance.
